newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINLAND'S AHTISAARI TO CONTINUE BUSINESS PROMOTION.
newsitem.headline: FINLAND'S AHTISAARI TO CONTINUE BUSINESS PROMOTION.

text.p: President Martti Ahtisaari said on Thursday he intended to continue travelling abroad to promote Finnish business since it is the best contribution he can make to help solve the unemployment problem.

Speaking at a rare news conference at his summer residence Kultaranta in the south-western town of Naantali ahead of his 60th birthday on Monday, he said the second half of his term would follow the path of the first half.
"On the whole, I will continue with the things I have done," he said.
"I will continue to promote business, since it is the best I can do for employment."
He said he would also continue travelling across the country to meet the people -- provincial trips he has been both praised and criticised for.
"I have heard no criticism from business life about my travels, if there was any, there would not be a single trip," Ahtisaari said.

Finland has a more stable political situation than most of Europe, and the government was very likely to rule its entire term until the next general elections in 1999, he said, and declined to give any preference regarding the next government base.
"I will, as I did last time (after the 1995 polls), let the process function, as it should," he said.
The president appoints the government and has the right to dissolve parliament and call new elections, should the parliament base not make possible a stable government.

He is also in charge of foreign policy jointly with the government, while in domestic policy, his powers are mostly indirect, although he formally sends bills to parliament and signs approved legislation into law and also appoints many top officials, the judges, officers and professors.

Ahtisaari, a social democrat with no previous political experience at home but a long carreer within the UN, took office in 1994 after he beat the Swedish People's Party's Elisabeth Rehn in the second round of elections.
He declined to say whether he planned to run for a second term in the next presidential elections in 2000.
"I spend more time thinking about my afternoon golf," he said.

Ahtisaari said the planned third stage of economic and monetary union (EMU) had less impact on security policy than generally believed, and that its impact on security would come through closer integration overall.
"The better the European economic development is, the better chances it creates for the EU's expansion," he said, adding this could help further NATO expansion.
